$about: THE canonical DeviceChain brand values. Every other representation is
GENERATED from this file — see tools/generate.mjs and the css/ directory.
Edit here, run `npm run generate -w @devicechain/brand`, commit the result.
Values are stored as hex because the brandmark artwork is hex
(branding/logo.svg). HSL forms are DERIVED, never hand-written: the console
previously declared the brand blue as the rounded triple `197 71% 42%`,
which renders #1f8cb7 and is therefore not the same colour as the #208cb7
in the artwork. Deriving removes that class of mismatch entirely.

primary.role: Brand blue. The logo's "CHAIN" wordmark and cube. THE interactive colour — the only one that ever means "you can click this".

primaryBright.role: Primary lifted for dark grounds and hover states.
primaryBright.$note: Reconciles a real three-way divergence. The console (dark `hsl(197 71% 49%)`) and the docs (dark `#24a3d6`) already agreed on this value; the marketing site had drifted to #3aa9d4 = hsl(197 64% 53%), which is visibly lighter and less saturated. Console is the documented source of truth and carried the majority, so it wins. Applying this to the website is a VISIBLE change to hover states and the hero eyebrow and must be reviewed on its own.

primaryDeep.role: Deepest cube facet. Navy, used for grounds rather than text.

primaryPale.role: Lightest cube facet. Highlights and hairlines.

bg.role: Default dark canvas — the "devicechain.io treatment" ground.

bgDeep.role: Deeper canvas for pages carrying the hex field.
bgDeep.$note: LOAD-BEARING: must equal the hex-field renderer's gl.clearColor. If they differ, distant fogged tiles read as a dark silhouette against a lighter sky instead of dissolving into it.

ink2.role: Secondary prose — ledes and section body.

$about: The expanded graphical language. The core palette above is a single hue —
every swatch sits between 197 and 207 — which is why the brand reads as
consistent but flat. These five stops walk monotonically THROUGH the
anchor blue rather than away from it, so each product area gets its own
identity without any of them fighting the brand.
ONE RULE, and it is the whole system: core.primary is the only colour that
ever means "interactive". An accent identifies an AREA. It never marks a
link, a button or a control. Break that and the page stops being
Order is pipeline order: ingest -> detect -> react -> command.

amber.$note: Also the deliberate antidote to reading a product called DeviceChain as web3 — warm is the one thing that palette never is.

sans.value: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
sans.$note: Placeholder stack. A real display/body pairing is still an open brand decision; the hero's headline sizing is currently tuned against whatever system-ui resolves to and will need re-tuning when a webfont lands.

mono.value: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "DejaVu Sans Mono", "Liberation Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace
